chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim and Ibn Muskhan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: We asked him

about a person in ihram who trod upon an ostrich egg and crushed it. He said: 'He sends a male [animal] in place of the number of eggs from the sheep, just as he sends a male in place of the number of eggs from the camels.'

key_terms.الْفَحْلَ: A male animal (used here for compensation)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally crushing an ostrich egg while in ihram?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the fidya for accidentally crushing an ostrich egg while in ihram. The Imam establishes a proportional compensation by sending a male animal for each egg, mirroring the established logic for other livestock, which highlights the juristic principle of applying consistent quantitative metrics to diverse forms of accidental damage during pilgrimage.
